content.text: {"primary_meaning":"When used symbolically, “uncircumcised” most commonly denotes a person or human nature not inwardly consecrated to God—especially a hardened, disobedient, spiritually insensitive heart that remains identified with the “flesh” rather than covenant faithfulness.","primary_basis":["Deuteronomy 10:16 — Israel is commanded to circumcise the foreskin of the heart and cease being stubborn.","Deuteronomy 30:6 — God promises to circumcise the heart so that his people will love him.","Jeremiah 4:4 — circumcision of the heart is associated with repentance and removal of evil.","Jeremiah 6:10 — an “uncircumcised ear” is unable or unwilling to hear God's word.","Jeremiah 9:25–26 — physical circumcision is contrasted with being uncircumcised in heart.","Ezekiel 44:7,9 — uncircumcision of heart and flesh marks unfitness for sanctuary access.","Acts 7:51 — “uncircumcised in heart and ears” describes persistent resistance to the Holy Spirit.","Romans 2:25–29 — inward circumcision of the heart is contrasted with merely outward circumcision.","Colossians 2:11–13 — spiritual circumcision is described as putting off the body of flesh and is connected with union with Christ.","Philippians 3:3 — believers are identified as the true circumcision through worship by the Spirit and confidence in Christ rather than the flesh."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Literal covenantal or ethnic status: the foreskin simply indicates that a male has not received Israel's physical covenant sign, and “the uncircumcised” can function as a designation for Gentiles or covenant outsiders rather than as an independent symbol of personal depravity.","basis":["Genesis 17:9–14","Joshua 5:2–9","1 Samuel 17:26,36","Ephesians 2:11–12"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Moral impurity, profaneness, or unfitness to approach what is holy. This overlaps with covenant exclusion but emphasizes ritual or sacred-space incompatibility.","basis":["Isaiah 52:1","Ezekiel 28:10","Ezekiel 31:18","Ezekiel 44:7,9"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Incapacity or impediment: metaphorical “uncircumcision” of lips or ears signifies ineffective speech, inability to hear, or resistance to receiving God's message.","basis":["Exodus 6:12,30","Jeremiah 6:10","Acts 7:51"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Shame and reproach associated with uncircumcision, particularly in narratives where circumcision marks incorporation into Israel and removal of disgrace.","basis":["Genesis 34:14","Joshua 5:9","1 Samuel 17:26"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"A typological contrast between old-covenant circumcision and Christian baptism or union with Christ, with removal of the foreskin interpreted as foreshadowing the putting away of sinful flesh.","basis":["Colossians 2:11–13","Romans 6:3–6"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Physical circumcision and uncircumcision are spiritually indifferent under the new covenant; what matters is faith, obedience, or new creation. Here uncircumcision is not assigned an inherently negative symbolic value.","basis":["1 Corinthians 7:18–19","Galatians 5:6","Galatians 6:15","Colossians 3:11"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a strong consensus about the metaphorical phrases “uncircumcised heart” and “uncircumcised ears”: they signify stubbornness, spiritual insensitivity, or lack of inward covenant faithfulness. Nevertheless, “foreskin” or “uncircumcised” by itself has no single settled symbolic meaning across all biblical contexts. It may be literal, denote Gentile or covenant-outside status, express impurity or shame, or serve Pauline contrasts concerning flesh and inward renewal."}
